title: NVIDIA H100 SXM
summary: The datacenter workhorse: 80 GB HBM3, ~989 TFLOPS BF16 dense, 4th-gen Tensor Cores.
details: The H100 SXM (Hopper) delivers about 989 TFLOPS of BF16 dense compute (nearly 2 PFLOPS with FP8), 80 GB of HBM3 at 3 TB/s, and 900 GB/s NVLink. It trained most frontier models of 2023-2025 and remains the reference GPU for training economics. The PCIe variant trades some bandwidth for server compatibility. Fourth-gen Tensor Cores add the Transformer Engine with automatic FP8 mixed precision.

demo.title: H100 training throughput
demo.program:
tflops, mfu = 989, 0.45
print(f"effective: {tflops*mfu:.0f} TFLOPS/GPU")
print(f"8-GPU node: {8*tflops*mfu/1000:.1f} PFLOPS effective")

title: NVIDIA H200
summary: H100-class compute with 141 GB HBM3e — the memory-capacity upgrade for long context.
details: The H200 keeps Hopper compute but upgrades memory to 141 GB of HBM3e at 4.8 TB/s — 76% more capacity and 43% more bandwidth than H100. For inference, that means longer contexts and bigger batches per GPU; for training, larger models per node. It slots into existing HGX H100 systems, making it a drop-in upgrade path.

demo.title: H200 context capacity
demo.program:
mem_gb, per_token_kb = 141, 1.0  # ~1MB/token for 70B-ish KV
print(f"max KV tokens: {mem_gb*1e6/per_token_kb/1e6:.1f}M tokens (rough)")

title: NVIDIA B200
summary: Blackwell flagship: 192 GB HBM3e, ~2.2 PFLOPS BF16 dense, 5th-gen Tensor Cores with FP4.
details: The B200 (Blackwell) roughly doubles H100 training throughput: ~2.2 PFLOPS BF16 dense, 192 GB HBM3e at 8 TB/s, and new FP4 precision for inference. Two B200 dies are co-packaged per GPU. It anchors the GB200 NVL72 rack systems and DGX B200 nodes — the platform for 2025-era frontier training.

demo.title: B200 vs H100
demo.program:
for name, tflops in [("H100", 989), ("B200", 2250)]:
    print(f"{name}: {tflops} TFLOPS BF16")

title: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72
summary: A full rack as one GPU: 72 B200s with NVLink-domain memory pooling — 130 TB/s fabric.
details: The GB200 NVL72 connects 72 Blackwell GPUs (36 Grace CPU + 72 GPU 'superchips') in a single NVLink domain with 130 TB/s aggregate bandwidth, presenting as one giant accelerator with ~13.5 TB of pooled HBM3e. It enables trillion-parameter MoE inference in one rack and 30x faster real-time inference claims versus H100 systems on certain workloads. This is rack-scale computing: the unit is the rack, not the card.

demo.title: NVL72 pooled memory
demo.program:
gpus, mem = 72, 192
print(f"pooled: {gpus*mem/1024:.1f} TB HBM3e in one NVLink domain")

title: NVIDIA A100
summary: The previous-gen workhorse: 40/80 GB HBM2e, still everywhere in research and inference.
details: The A100 (Ampere) delivers 312 TFLOPS BF16 dense with 40 or 80 GB HBM2e at 2 TB/s. Though superseded by Hopper, A100s remain the most common research GPU — cheaper on spot markets, ample for fine-tuning and inference of 7-70B models. The 80GB variant with NVLink still trains serious models; it is the value tier of datacenter AI.

demo.title: A100 value check

title: NVIDIA L40S
summary: The universal datacenter GPU: Ada Lovelace power for inference, graphics, and fine-tuning.
details: The L40S packs 48 GB GDDR6 and strong FP8/FP16 throughput in a passively cooled PCIe card that fits standard servers — no SXM baseboard needed. It targets inference, fine-tuning, and graphics/AI mixed workloads, delivering near-H100 inference performance per dollar in many deployments. The easy drop-in form factor made it the default inference GPU for enterprises.

demo.title: L40S inference fit
demo.program:
mem = 48
print(f"fits 70B Q4 ({70*0.5:.0f}GB) + KV cache comfortably")

title: AMD Instinct MI300X
summary: AMD's H100 challenger: 192 GB HBM3 per GPU — the memory king of its generation.
details: The MI300X offers 192 GB of HBM3 (5.3 TB/s) per GPU — 2.4x the H100's memory — with ~1.3 PFLOPS BF16 dense. Its headline advantage: run 70B+ models on fewer GPUs. Software (ROCm) has matured substantially, with vLLM and PyTorch support now solid. Deployed at scale by Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle clouds, it is the first credible datacenter alternative to NVIDIA for LLM serving.

demo.title: MI300X memory advantage
demo.program: print(f"MI300X {192}GB vs H100 {80}GB = {192/80:.1f}x memory per GPU")

title: AMD Instinct MI325X
summary: MI300X refresh with 256 GB HBM3e — AMD's answer to H200.
details: The MI325X bumps memory to 256 GB HBM3e at 6 TB/s with the same CDNA 3 compute, targeting H200-class inference workloads. Same platform compatibility as MI300X for easy upgrades. AMD's roadmap continues to MI350 (CDNA 4) with FP4/FP6 support.

title: Google TPU v5e
summary: Google's efficient inference/training TPU — the cost-per-chip leader in its class.
details: TPU v5e is Google's balanced-generation TPU: strong BF16 throughput per dollar and per watt, designed for both training and inference at Google scale (it trained Gemini-era models alongside v5p). Available on Google Cloud, it appeals to cost-sensitive training with XLA/JAX tooling. The trade-off is ecosystem: JAX/XLA first, PyTorch via XLA second.

demo.title: TPU pod scale
demo.program:
chips = 256
print(f"v5e pod slice: {chips} chips, ~{chips*197/1000:.0f} PFLOPS BF16")

title: Google TPU v5p
summary: Google's flagship training TPU pod — thousands of chips for frontier runs.
details: TPU v5p is Google's most powerful training TPU: 3D torus interconnect, large HBM, and pod-scale deployment in the thousands of chips. It trained production Gemini models. Like all TPUs it is cloud-only (no on-prem purchase), and peak efficiency comes from JAX/XLA programs written TPU-aware.

demo.title: v5p pod math
demo.program:
chips = 4096
print(f"{chips} chips x 459 TFLOPS = {chips*459/1e6:.1f} exaFLOPS BF16")

title: AWS Trainium2
summary: Amazon's second-gen training chip — purpose-built for AWS-scale model training.
details: Trainium2 (Trn2) powers EC2 Trn2 instances and UltraServers (up to 64 chips with NeuronLink interconnect), delivering 3-4x the performance of Trainium1 for LLM training. It runs via the AWS Neuron SDK (PyTorch/XLA-based). The pitch is price-performance on AWS: competitive training throughput at lower $/FLOP than GPUs, for teams already on AWS.

demo.program:
chips = 64
print(f"UltraServer: {chips} Trainium2, NeuronLink interconnect")

title: AWS Inferentia2
summary: Amazon's inference chip: high throughput per dollar for deployed models.
details: Inferentia2 (Inf2) targets inference with NeuronCores optimized for transformer decode, large on-chip SRAM, and strong perf-per-dollar on EC2 Inf2 instances. It serves 70B-class models across multiple chips with tensor parallelism via the Neuron SDK. The value proposition is sustained inference cost, not peak flexibility.
memory: 32 GB HBM per chip (x6 per instance)

demo.program:

print(f"inf2.48xlarge: {chips} chips, {chips*mem} GB HBM")

title: Intel Gaudi 3
summary: Intel's third-gen AI accelerator: open Ethernet networking, strong price-performance claims.
details: Gaudi 3 offers 128 GB HBM2e, ~1.8 PFLOPS BF16, and notably uses standard Ethernet (RoCE) for scale-out instead of proprietary fabrics — cheaper clustering. Intel claims competitive perf-per-dollar versus H100 for LLM training and inference, with PyTorch-native software. Available on Intel Tiber Cloud and IBM Cloud.

demo.title: Gaudi3 networking advantage
demo.program: print("24x 200GbE ports on-card: no proprietary switch tax")

title: Cerebras WSE-3
summary: The wafer-scale engine: one giant chip with 4 trillion transistors for fast training.
details: Cerebras WSE-3 is a wafer-scale chip — the entire silicon wafer is one processor with 900,000 cores and 44 GB of on-chip SRAM, delivering extreme memory bandwidth for its size. The CS-3 system targets fast training of large models with weight-streaming execution. It is the most radical architectural bet in AI hardware: kill the memory wall by never leaving the wafer.

echo "CS-3 system: weight-streaming execution, no off-chip bottleneck

title: Groq LPU
summary: The inference-speed king: deterministic low-latency token generation on a custom LPU.
details: Groq's Language Processing Unit is a deterministic, single-core-streaming architecture that compiles the whole model onto the chip — no external memory fetches during decode. Result: 500+ tokens/sec on Llama-70B-class models with single-digit-ms latency. Available via GroqCloud API; the trade-off is model-size limits per card and a compile-per-model flow.
memory: 230 MB on-chip SRAM per chip (model sharded)

demo.title: Groq speed math
demo.program:
tps, tokens = 500, 1000
print(f"1000 tokens in {tokens/tps:.0f}s vs ~50s on typical GPU serving")

title: SambaNova SN40L
summary: Reconfigurable dataflow for trillion-parameter models — 12 TB DDR memory per node.
details: SambaNova's SN40L uses a reconfigurable dataflow architecture with 3-tier memory (HBM + DDR + on-chip), offering 12 TB of DDR per 8-chip node — enough to hold trillion-parameter models for inference. Their Samba-1 cloud and on-prem systems target large-model inference and fine-tuning with a full software stack.

demo.program: print("12 TB DDR/node: trillion-parameter models fit for inference")

title: Graphcore Bow IPU
summary: IPU with in-processor memory: thousands of cores each with local SRAM.
details: Graphcore's Bow IPU packs 1,472 cores each with local SRAM (900 MB total per chip) in a 3D-stacked design, running at higher clocks than its predecessor. The IPU excels at fine-grained parallel workloads and sparse models; the programming model (Poplar) differs from CUDA, which has limited adoption versus the GPU ecosystem.

demo.program: print("900MB on-chip: keep working set local, stream the rest")

title: NVIDIA RTX 4090
summary: The consumer flagship that moonlights as an AI workstation card: 24 GB, fast, everywhere.
details: The RTX 4090 (Ada Lovelace) offers 24 GB GDDR6X and ~330 TFLOPS FP16 dense — enough to fine-tune 7B models (QLoRA) and run 70B quantized inference. Its ubiquity and price (~$1,600 MSRP) made it the default for local AI development, Vast.ai rentals, and small inference servers. The 24GB ceiling is its limit for bigger models.

demo.program: print("7B QLoRA fine-tune: fits | 70B Q4 inference: fits | 70B fp16: no")

title: Apple M3 Neural Engine
summary: On-device AI for a billion devices: 18 TOPS in the M3's neural engine.
details: Apple's M3 Neural Engine delivers 18 trillion operations/sec for on-device ML (Core ML, transformers via ANE), with unified memory (up to 128 GB on Max) letting large models run locally. It powers Private Cloud Compute's on-device side and the growing local-LLM scene on Macs. The lesson: serious AI now ships in laptops.

demo.program: print("M3 Max 128GB: 70B Q4 (~40GB) runs locally via llama.cpp/MLX")

title: Qualcomm Cloud AI 100
summary: Qualcomm's datacenter inference card: performance per watt for sustained serving.
details: The Cloud AI 100 targets inference with strong perf-per-watt, PCIe form factor, and support via the Qualcomm Cloud AI SDK. Newer Ultra variants raise throughput for generative AI. It serves cost-sensitive inference deployments, especially at the edge-datacenter boundary.

title: d-Matrix Corsair
summary: Digital in-memory compute for inference: MAC operations inside the memory array.
details: d-Matrix's Corsair uses digital in-memory computing (DIMC) — multiply-accumulate inside SRAM arrays — targeting LLM inference with high tokens-per-watt. Backed by Microsoft investment, it aims at the datacenter inference efficiency gap. Representative of the in-memory compute wave challenging von Neumann bottlenecks.

demo.program: print("MAC inside SRAM: no weight-movement energy per op")

title: NVIDIA H800
summary: The export-compliant H100 variant: capped interconnect for regulated markets.
details: The H800 is NVIDIA's China-market H100: same Hopper compute with interconnect bandwidth capped to meet export controls. It keeps most training capability for domestic workloads while complying with regulations. Illustrates how geopolitics now shapes accelerator SKUs directly.

demo.title: H800 vs H100
demo.program: print("compute: same class | NVLink: capped | market: export-compliant")

title: AMD MI210
summary: The previous-gen AMD datacenter GPU: 64 GB HBM2e, ROCm-mature, value inference.
details: The MI210 (CDNA 2) offers 64 GB HBM2e and solid FP16/BF16 throughput with mature ROCm support. Older than MI300X but widely available and cheaper — a value option for inference and fine-tuning in AMD-friendly stacks.

title: Google TPU v4
summary: The TPU that trained PaLM: optical interconnect pods at massive scale.
details: TPU v4 pods (4,096 chips) with optical circuit switching trained PaLM and other Google flagships. Still widely used on Google Cloud for training and inference, v4 remains a workhorse behind v5's halo. Demonstrates Google's pod-scale philosophy: thousands of chips, one job.

title: NVIDIA GH200 Superchip
summary: Grace CPU + Hopper GPU on one package: 480 GB coherent memory for giant models.
details: The GH200 fuses a Grace ARM CPU (480 GB LPDDR5X) with an H100 GPU (96 GB HBM3) via 900 GB/s NVLink-C2C, presenting ~600 GB of coherent memory. For inference of huge models and CPU-GPU unified workloads (RAG with big vector stores), the coherent pool beats discrete cards. The GB200 successor extends the concept to Blackwell.

demo.program: print("600GB coherent: 70B fp16 (140GB) + 400GB vector store, one node")
